# MCR scorer provenance and build

Upstream: Jeff Wang, [ChineseOfficialMahjongHelper](https://github.com/summerinsects/ChineseOfficialMahjongHelper), `Classes/mahjong-algorithm`, commit `7872fa2573f649afabdca7f96cc253e5bb4366fa` (MIT, 2016–2023). The unabridged license is in LICENSE and each source. OpenMahjong's surrounding implementation remains AGPL-3.0-only.

The selected rules are the **WMO 2006 English MCR edition hosted by EMA**: https://mahjong-europe.org/portal/images/docs/mcr_EN.pdf . This is a named, frozen edition, not a claim of tournament certification or the latest amendment. Local header patches: set Two Concealed Kongs to eight points; represent the concealed-plus-melded kong combination specified under pattern 57 as six points, using the upstream internal combination slot rather than the later five-point value; expose the upstream English names. The public catalog retains 81 patterns; the derived combination is separately labeled in scoring breakdowns. The bridge and TypeScript boundary are original OpenMahjong work. No annual American card material is included.

`scripts/build-mcr-scorer.sh` rebuilds the checked-in `src/variants/mcr-runtime.ts` with Emscripten **3.1.64**, pure JavaScript (`WASM=0`), a fixed 16 MiB heap and a synchronous, lazy factory. Ordinary Node/browser builds need no compiler, downloaded binary, network service, runtime fetch, or credentials. The generated code carries this notice; readable corresponding sources, bridge and build instructions ship in the engine package. Standard Emscripten glue contains unused resource-loading functions; no external resource is requested by the embedded runtime.

Tests use separately constructed hands and payment arithmetic, including exclusions, eight-fan eligibility and special structures. The scorer maximizes a legal decomposition under the upstream exclusion/non-repeat implementation. Its strategic use remains a public-information heuristic, never an outcome-based grade.
